title: Committee recommendations approved; budget deliberations unfinished
subtitle: Child care leases, affordable housing, waste transfer tender, Metrolinx land sale, speed cameras, and Wilmont land assembly concerns.
overview: Regional Council approved a broad set of items {{vote:m7}}, including committee recommendations on a sale of Region-owned land in Kitchener to Metrolinx, the Victoria Street North design, a Duke Street West road transfer, a Petersburg water charge by-law, and amendments to the traffic by-law supporting the municipal speed camera program from January 1, 2025.

Council also approved a priority affordable rental housing project {{vote:m3}}, a six-year waste transfer contract for the Cambridge and Waterloo facilities {{vote:m4}}, and leases for two non-profit child care centres in Cambridge {{vote:m5}} {{vote:m6}}. Councillor Colleen James was appointed to the City of Waterloo Town and Gown Committee {{vote:m10}}.

Two delegates spoke against the proposed Wilmont land assembly, citing a lack of consultation and transparency and a lack of environmental review. The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee did not finish the 2025 budget. A motion to extend past midnight was defeated, and the committee was set to resume on the morning of December 20, followed by a special Council meeting.

decisions.detail: Council approved the recommended priority project under the New Affordable Rental Housing program and authorized staff to sign funding agreements and documents with proponents.

Council accepted the tender of Dawson Contract Services Inc. for bulk transfer of waste from the Cambridge and Waterloo facilities, at an estimated $17,998,300 plus taxes over six years, with options to renew.
Council authorized a five-year lease, with two five-year renewal terms, for Tender Loving Daycare to run a non-profit child care centre in Cambridge.

decisions.item: Indigenous-led child care and housing partnerships
decisions.detail: Council authorized a lease at 30 Christopher Drive, Cambridge, for an Indigenous-led non-profit child care centre and directed staff to explore affordable housing partnerships with non-profit and private sectors.

Council approved the sale of Region-owned land at 16 Victoria Street North to Metrolinx for $1,434,000, the Victoria Street North preliminary design, a Petersburg water charge by-law, a tax increment grant assignment for 49 Queen Street East, Cambridge, and traffic by-law changes including for the speed camera program.
Councillor Colleen James was appointed to the City of Waterloo Inter-Agency Town and Gown Committee.

debate: Two delegates opposed the Wilmont land assembly. They raised the lack of public consultation, the confidentiality around the process, and the absence of published studies or costing. One tied it to provincial planning criticisms and to tariff uncertainty.

A second delegate said the land acknowledgment should lead to action. The delegate asked for environmental and water impact surveys and consultation with the Grand River Conservation Authority and farmers.

During the budget committee, a councillor proposed capping growth in supplies, equipment, facilities, professional fees, communications, travel and occupancy costs at 5%. The councillor said the combined 9.32% increase well exceeded inflation, and left it to staff to find the reductions.

Staff said they had only seen the motion about an hour earlier and could not fully assess the risks. They said many increases reflected full-year effects of 2024 decisions and construction inflation running above the standard consumer price index. One councillor called a reduction of roughly $7 million at the last hour too much and suggested about $2 million.

Another councillor called the late-night process chaotic and said the budget should be done properly with staff input. This led to a motion to extend past midnight, which was defeated, and to the decision to continue on a later date.
